deviation: The draft drops the termination right after a prolonged force majeure event, so Arcadia could be stuck with an indefinitely suspended supplier. It also broadens force majeure to cover labour disputes, utility/telecom failures, third-party network or cloud outages and cyber-attacks, and it doesn't exclude supplier staffing or subcontractor failures. This lets the supplier excuse risks it should manage itself.
suggested_text:
17.1 Neither party is liable for delay in performing its obligations (other than payment obligations) caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided that it notifies the other party promptly and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance. Supplier staffing shortages, labour disputes involving Supplier's or its subcontractors' personnel, and failures or delays of Supplier's subcontractors or suppliers are not events beyond Supplier's reasonable control. Failures of third-party networks, cloud services, utilities or telecommunications, and cyber-attacks, are not force majeure events to the extent they could have been prevented by Supplier's compliance with this Agreement or by reasonable business continuity, disaster recovery or security measures.

17.2 Either party may terminate the affected services on written notice, without liability, if the force majeure event continues for more than 60 days.
